prompt_text: Who is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City to help me pick a plan?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t honestly name one single “best” broker — that depends on what kind of coverage you need (individual/family, ACA marketplace, Medicare, small‑group/employer plan), whether you prefer an independent broker or a captive agent, and other preferences (in‑person help, language, fees). If you tell me what type of plan you need and your ZIP code, I can pull up local options and narrow the list. Meanwhile, here’s a quick, practical way to find a great broker in Kansas City and vet them.

Quick questions
- Are you shopping for individual/family, ACA (marketplace), Medicare, or employer group coverage?
- Which side of KC are you on — Missouri or Kansas (ZIP)? Do you prefer an in‑person meeting?
- Any important needs (bilingual, chronic conditions, narrow network doctors, budget)?

How to find good brokers
- For Medicare: use Medicare.gov “Find Local Help” or call 1‑800‑MEDICARE to locate certified SHIP counselors and licensed agents.
- For ACA/individual plans: use HealthCare.gov’s agent/broker finder or local independent brokers who handle marketplace plans.
- For employer/small group: search for local benefits brokers who specialize in small businesses.
- Nationwide broker directories: NAHU (National Association of Health Underwriters) “Find an Agent.”
- Local search: Google Maps, Yelp, Nextdoor — look for firms with many recent positive reviews and experience in the plan type you need.

How to vet and compare brokers (ask these questions)
- Are you licensed in Kansas and Missouri? (Ask for license number and verify on state insurance department sites.)
- Do you work independent or are you tied to one insurance carrier? (Independent is usually better for comparing multiple carriers.)
- How are you compensated? (Commission from insurers vs. fee-for-service; ask if they charge clients directly.)
- What plans/carriers do you commonly work with in KC?
- Do you help with enrollment, claims, appeals, and annual plan reviews?
- Can you provide references from clients with similar needs?
- How long have you been doing this and what professional certifications do you hold?

Red flags
- Pressure to sign immediately or only one carrier offered.
- No clear answer on licensing or compensation.
- Poor or no online reviews and no references.

Verify credentials and complaints
- Missouri Department of Commerce & Insurance license lookup
- Kansas Insurance Department license lookup
- Better Business Bureau and consumer review sites

If you want, give me:
- ZIP code
- Type of coverage (Medicare, ACA, individual/family, small business)
- Any special preferences (in‑person, language, help with claims)

I’ll find several well‑rated local brokers and give a short vetted list with contact details and reasons to consider each.
